qa_pairs.question: How do you start or resume a Rocky simulation using a GPU on an Alliance cluster?
qa_pairs.answer: To start a new Rocky simulation using a GPU on an Alliance cluster, set the `RESUME` variable to `0` in your Slurm script. This will remove any previous simulation results and initiate a fresh run with the command `Rocky --headless --simulate --resume=0 --ncpus=$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK --use-gpu=1 $INPUTFILE`. To resume a partially completed Rocky simulation, set the `RESUME` variable to `1`, which will execute `Rocky --headless --simulate --resume=1 --ncpus=$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK --use-gpu=1 $INPUTFILE`.

qa_pairs.question: What is the function of the `RESUME` variable in a Rocky simulation script?
qa_pairs.answer: The `RESUME` variable in a Rocky simulation script dictates whether the simulation will start from the beginning or continue from a previous state. When `RESUME=0`, any prior simulation results are deleted (`rm -rf $INPUTFILE.files/simulation`), and the simulation is started anew. When `RESUME=1`, the simulation attempts to resume from its last checkpoint.
